## Reflection

I called DNA damage at 0.45 because 4 wells showed a consistent dose-dependent large pale-nucleus signal — nuc_major_axis up to z=+10.3 rho +1.00 and nuc_dna_mean down to z=-6.1 rho -1.00 — with NSC 3/4 voting DNA damage and decreasing mitotic fraction. What was right:
- Correctly excluded mitotic/cytoskeletal MoAs (Aurora, Eg5, microtubule destabilizers, actin disruptors) using intact filaments, no multinucleation on describe_phenotype, and frac_mitotic_like decreasing with dose rho -0.95.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted NSC 3/4 majority from compare_to_reference_atlas despite very low similarities 0.252-0.325; discrimination from Protein degradation (1 vote, k-neighbours 3/10) rested on vote count, not biology.
- Misinterpreted dose-dependent large pale nuclei and lower density (e2, e3, e7, e8, e11, e12, e16) as DNA-damage specific, missing that p38 kinase inhibition also regulates antiproliferative p21 and proliferation/differentiation programs.
